clue.text: So, taxis on rank outside pub; one sounding horn

indicators.note: rank here is an adjective meaning foul or corrupt, so the preceding words are spoilt into a new order
the rearranged letters stand outside, wrapping round the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter as fodder
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A queue of cabs at a rank waits outside a pub while one driver leans on the horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The horn in the surface is a car's; in the definition it is the sax, a jazz horn, so SAXOPHONIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz players call any wind instrument a horn, so a player blowing a sax is one sounding a horn.

clue.text: Support minor criminal in old age?

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it
a minor is someone under age
a hood is a gangster, short for hoodlum

explanation.surface: Backing a young offender seems an odd thing to do in one's dotage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the phrase is used of elderly people behaving childishly, not of old age itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Second childhood is the idiom for the dependent, childlike state of very elderly people, so it stands for senility.

clue.text: People in south taken in by foolish hoax

indicators.note: a foolish version of a word is a silly, muddled one, so its letters get mixed up
taken in by means swallowed or enclosed, so the compass point sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Southerners fooled by a silly prank.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' after People is only a link; the S goes inside the jumbled hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: The Xhosa are a Bantu nation of South Africa, so the name denotes an ethnic group, a people.

clue.text: First woman occasionally read letters for Post Office on top

indicators.note: in a down answer on top places the first piece above the second
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the initials of Post Office are P and O, written out with the word and
the first and third letters of read

explanation.surface: A woman reads her letters only now and then, and posts them first.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is spelling the initials as 'P and O' in full; the first woman is from Greek myth, not Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora was the first mortal woman, made by the gods and given the fateful jar.

clue.text: Slower operator holding up old phone company

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece holding something up sits underneath it, so the operator comes last

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
BT is British Telecom, the UK's main telephone company
a user is someone who operates something

explanation.surface: A switchboard operator delaying calls with the old phone company.
explanation.walkthrough: BT, formerly British Telecom, is the UK's main phone firm. 'Slower' means slower on the uptake, not in speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means dull-witted, so someone more obtuse is slower to understand.

clue.text: Wearing spectacles to show wisdom

definitions.note: the answer is plural; the definition is a mass noun

blocks.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'
sights are spectacles, things worth seeing

explanation.surface: Putting on glasses to look wise.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectacles look like glasses, but here they are sights, remarkable things to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Insights are deep understandings of things, which together amount to wisdom or perceptiveness.

clue.text: Regularly told migraine affected face: it's connected with facial muscles

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept
affected means disturbed or altered, so these letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: the first and third letters of told
taken letter for letter as fodder
to face something is to brave it, and nerve as a verb means to brace oneself

explanation.surface: A patient reports that a migraine has spread to their face, a medical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like the place the migraine struck, but it is a verb: to face or brave something is to nerve yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: The trigeminal is the fifth cranial nerve, carrying sensation from the face and driving the chewing muscles.

clue.text: Seeing caramel in order for custard

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them properly, so the jumble is sorted into a new word

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Spotting caramel on the menu and ordering some custard to go with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème anglaise is the French name for a thin vanilla pouring sauce made of eggs, sugar and milk, which is custard.

clue.text: Guessing John, finally is eighty: posh spread?

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the name is kept
spread means scattered about, so all the gathered letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of John
taken as written
taken letter for letter as fodder
taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Speculating that John turns eighty and gets a fancy party.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'posh spread' looks like a lavish buffet; spread is the anagram signal for everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hypothesise is to put forward a theory without proof, which is to make an educated guess.

clue.text: Being in America fancy that new motor, retiring earlier

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word for motor is read backwards
earlier tells us the turned-round motor goes at the front of the other pieces

blocks.note: a motor is a car
coo is an exclamation of surprise, like fancy that
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone in the States is amazed by a new car pulling away.
explanation.walkthrough: RAC + COO + N gives RACCOON. 'Being' is the noun, a living creature, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon is a mammal native to North America, so it is a living creature found in the States.

clue.text: Swear whenever irritable drinking

indicators.note: something drinking takes a thing inside itself, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: testy means short-tempered
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: Someone who curses whenever they get cross after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swear' looks like cursing in the surface, but it is the solemn kind made in a witness box.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to state something on oath in court, which is to swear to it.

clue.text: They order madras, not when drunk

indicators.note: drunk things stagger about, so the letters before it lurch into a new arrangement

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Curry-house diners who avoid ordering a madras when they have had a few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They order' sounds like customers ordering food; it means people who issue commands.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandator is someone who issues a mandate, an authoritative command, so mandators are people giving instructions.

clue.text: Heavy metal fan to leave gathering on bike at front

indicators.note: at front keeps only the opening letter of the vehicle word
gathering means collecting in, so the verb for leaving encloses what follows

blocks.note: to go is to leave
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
the first letter of bike

explanation.surface: A rocker ditches a get-together and roars off on a motorbike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To leave gathering' reads like walking out of a meeting, but gathering is the containment signal, not the thing left.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebo is British slang for a long-haired fan of heavy metal or grunge music, often a biker.

clue.text: Bend ruler with no metres on

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the following parts are taken out of the ruler

blocks.note: a monarch is a ruling king or queen
M is the symbol for metres
taken as written

explanation.surface: A curved measuring rule with no metre markings on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M and ON out of MONARCH to leave ARCH. 'Ruler' looks like a measuring stick, which fits the metres, but it is a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: To arch is to curve into a bow shape, the same as bending, and an arch is itself a curved bend.

clue.text: This has chromatic scales for harpist to play

indicators.note: to play letters is to toy with them, so the fodder is reshuffled

blocks.note: both words taken letter by letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A piece with chromatic scales set for a harpist to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'for harpist', so 'for' is also part of the letters. Chromatic scales sound musical; here they are brightly coloured fish scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Parrotfish are reef fish famous for vividly coloured bodies, so their scales are literally chromatic, full of colour.

clue.text: Break crockery over on side

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for crockery is read backwards
in a down answer on means sitting on top of the next piece

blocks.note: pots are earthenware vessels, crockery
a side of paper is a page

explanation.surface: Smashing plates by knocking them over onto their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' suggests smashing the crockery, but it means a pause or interruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt in work or play, a break in proceedings.

clue.text: They're in fast car describing rubbish acceleration

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the car letters go round what follows

blocks.note: GTI is the badge on hot hatchbacks such as the Golf GTI
litter is rubbish left lying about
A is the physics symbol for acceleration

explanation.surface: Celebrities in a sports car, whose rubbish acceleration is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'They're in', meaning the in-crowd; the rest of the clue is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The glitterati are fashionable celebrities, the people who are in vogue, the in-crowd.

clue.text: Romeo escorts dashing people

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ushers escort people to their seats

explanation.surface: Romeo accompanies some debonair folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing' looks like stylish, but here it means hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusher is someone who hurries, so rushers are people dashing about.

clue.text: Part of victim panic-stricken: they're beaten with sticks

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a stretch of the following words, not all of them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A terrified victim being thrashed with sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: The sticks are drumsticks, not weapons, which turns the violent picture into an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums, played by striking them with padded mallets or drumsticks.

clue.text: Men in jazz show

blocks.note: first meaning: jazz slang for musicians or hip fellows
second meaning: the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: The musicians in a jazz show.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz slang calls players cool cats, and Cats is the long-running Lloyd Webber stage musical.

clue.text: Ring true legend, ultimately getting into a party

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept
getting into means entering, so the single letter goes inside the party

blocks.note: taken as written
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
the last letter of legend

explanation.surface: A famous figure's wedding ring sparks talk of joining a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party. 'Ring' is a verb here, as in sounding convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: When a story adds up it is consistent and makes sense, so it rings true.

clue.text: Old record label into rock's musical intervals

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the label sits within the rock word

blocks.note: rocks are stones, the 's read as a plural
EMI was a famous British record company

explanation.surface: A veteran record company getting into rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock looks like the music genre; the plural is just stones. EMI was the British label of the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest interval in Western music, the step between adjacent piano keys.

clue.text: Item for discussion along with image

blocks.note: to can mean in addition, as in adding one thing to another
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: An agenda item circulated together with a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject people talk or write about, a matter up for debate.

clue.text: Hold swingers at either side to screw

indicators.note: at either side picks an edge letter of the word, and both of its edges hold the same one

blocks.note: the letter found at both ends of swingers
taken as written
screw is old slang for wages or salary

explanation.surface: A racy invitation for wife-swapping couples.
explanation.walkthrough: Either side of swingers gives the same letter, so only one is needed. Screw as slang for pay is old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowage is space for stowing cargo, as in a ship's hold, so the two are the same storage area.

clue.text: Hopeful? Initially getting off painkillers

definitions.note: the answer is a mass noun; the definition is plural

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word
off means removed or taken away, so that letter is dropped from the end

blocks.note: an aspiring person hopes to achieve something
the first letter of getting

explanation.surface: Optimistic about getting off the painkillers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hopeful with its question mark looks like the definition; it is the source word losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, a common over-the-counter drug for relieving pain.

clue.text: Arrange band in part of theatre

blocks.note: to dress is to arrange, as in dressing a shop window
a band or ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Organising a group of musicians to play in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Band suggests musicians, but it is a ring shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress circle is the first raised tier of seats in a theatre, above the stalls.
